name: Farthest Reach

stars.name: Farthest Reach
stars.notes: Quiet, old main-sequence star with very low flare activity and a stable luminosity cycle

planets.name: Scald
planets.notes: Tidally locked scorched rock with a permanent magma lake on the dayside. No atmosphere remains.

planets.name: Farthest Reach II
planets.notes: Thin CO2 atmosphere over rust-colored desert plains. Ancient riverbeds suggest a wetter past billions of years ago.

planets.name: Cairnstone
planets.notes: Dense, iron-rich body with an unusually strong magnetic field for its size. Surface covered in metallic regolith.

planets.name: Outer Cairn
planets.notes: Nitrogen-methane ice world at the system's edge. Subsurface ocean suspected but unconfirmed by the single flyby survey.

anomalies.name: The Long Silence
anomalies.notes: An unexplained gravitational perturbation suggesting a missing planet or captured dark body. Automated probes sent to investigate have returned inconclusive data.

asteroid_belts.name: Cairnstone Ring
asteroid_belts.notes: Thin belt of silicate fragments, likely remnants of a failed protoplanet. Unremarkable mineral content.

faction_control.notes: Unclaimed. Cataloged by long-range survey drone; no faction has expressed territorial interest.

history: Detected by automated stellar cartography sweep in 2487, Farthest Reach was flagged only for its position at the extreme edge of the charted Outer Veil Expanse.

A single unmanned survey probe conducted a flyby in 2511, recording basic planetary data before continuing deeper into uncharted space. Its telemetry remains the only detailed observation of the system.
The gravitational anomaly between orbits 3 and 4 was noted in the probe's data but deemed low priority. No follow-up investigation has been funded or scheduled.
description: Farthest Reach is a quiet orange dwarf sitting at the ragged hem of explored space. Its four worlds are unremarkable individually — a scorched inner rock, a desiccated terrestrial, a dense metallic body, and a distant ice world — but together they form a complete if modest planetary system around a star that has burned steadily for over seven billion years. The light here is dim and warm, casting long shadows across worlds that have never known a human footprint.

No faction claims Farthest Reach, and no station orbits its worlds. The system's only significance is cartographic: it marks the farthest point of confirmed stellar survey along this particular vector of the Outer Veil Expanse. Passing ships occasionally use its star as a navigational reference when plotting courses into the deep unknown, but none linger.

The gravitational anomaly cataloged between the third and fourth orbits remains the system's single point of intrigue. The survey probe's instruments detected a mass shadow consistent with a planetary body, yet no object was observed. Whether this indicates a rogue dark body, an unusual density in the local interstellar medium, or simply instrument error aboard an aging probe is unknown. For now, the mystery sits filed in a database, waiting for someone with cause to look closer.
